title: Why the wave of protests sweeping Europe is unlike the mass mobilisation in 1968

ai.summary: The article compares the 2026 European protests to 1968, noting differences in protester grievances (state failures vs. demand for freedom), political outcomes, and violence. It highlights Serbia's student movement winning elections while France's protests led to political blame.

facts.quote: Spain’s November 11 general strike, called in response to a housing crisis, stagnant wages and rising living costs, is part of a much wider European story.

facts.claim: Serbia’s recent protest movement emerged after the 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy
facts.quote: Serbia’s recent protest movement suggests another trajectory. It emerged after the 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which became a symbol of wider corruption and accountability concerns.

facts.claim: Aleksandar Vučić dismissed the protesters as part of a western-backed 'colour revolution'
facts.quote: Aleksandar Vučić, the former Serbian president who was recently removed from power, dismissed the protesters as part of a western-backed "colour revolution".
